rounds.response:
Label the plate (ID, date, bench) and divide the agar bottom into four quadrants; flame-sterilize the loop and let it cool briefly (~5–10 s) before contacting the culture.  
Pick up a very small inoculum (single colony or a light dip in broth), streak quadrant 1 with 3–4 short parallel strokes, re-flame and cool the loop, then drag 2–3 streaks from Q1 into Q2; repeat flaming/cooling and a single gentle drag for Q2→Q3 and Q3→Q4 to progressively thin the inoculum.  
Keep the loop tip skimming the agar (do not gouge), minimize plate open time and hold the plate at a shallow angle to reduce contamination.  
Invert and incubate conservatively (e.g., ~30°C for 24–48 h or room temperature per instructor), record which quadrant yields isolated colonies, and discard materials per lab waste procedures.
